theory.overview: A hash table (hash map) is a data structure that implements an associative array abstract data type, mapping keys to values using a hash function. It provides O(1) average time complexity for insertions, deletions, and lookups. Collisions are handled via chaining (linked lists) or open addressing (probing). Hash tables are fundamental to databases, caches, compilers, and many high-performance applications.

keyConcepts.name: Hash Function
keyConcepts.description: Converts keys to array indices. A good hash function distributes keys uniformly to minimize collisions.

keyConcepts.name: Collision Resolution
keyConcepts.description: Chaining: store colliding elements in a linked list. Open Addressing: find next empty slot via probing.

keyConcepts.name: Load Factor
keyConcepts.description: Ratio of elements to buckets. When it exceeds a threshold (typically 0.75), the table resizes (rehashes).

keyConcepts.name: Rehashing
keyConcepts.description: Creating a larger table and reinserting all elements when load factor is too high. Expensive but amortized O(1).

problems.title: Minimum Index Sum of Two Lists
